text:
The scoreboard said seven, but the play said something closer to four. PIT generated 4.29 expected goals against PHI's 1.55, and Dan Vladar faced 38 shots with an expected goals against of 4.29, then allowed seven. That left him 2.71 goals worse than expected. PIT still deserved to win in 89 percent of simulated replays, so the margin was inflated, but the winner was never in doubt.

The first goal showed how loose the night would be for PHI. Nick Robertson tipped one home at 7:26 of the first on a 5 percent chance, and Ville Koivunen made it 2-0 with a backhand late in the period. The second period was where PIT took over, out-chancing PHI 1.85 to 0.51 in expected goals. Evgeni Malkin scored on the power play at 5:03, Hendrix Lapierre followed at 7:26, and Filip Hallander made it 5-0 at 10:23. Hallander finished with a goal and two assists in under 11 minutes of ice time, and his line was on the ice for 1.38 expected goals for against 0.39 against.

Robertson added a short-handed snap shot in the third for his second goal, and Egor Chinakhov closed the scoring on the power play at 16:37. PIT went 2 for 4 with the man advantage while PHI went 0 for 3. Arturs Silovs stopped all 19 shots he saw, 1.55 goals better than expected, and PHI also gave the puck away 21 times to PIT's 11.
